sd_test_piece_the.blurb: The Test Piece is a single, strikingly overhanging granite boulder in the Turtle Dome group on Iron Mountain, part of the Needles of Rushmore in the Black Hills. It carries eleven problems that cover a wide range, from easy V0 and V1 lines up to a couple of V6 and V7 test-pieces, with a few mid-grade problems between. Because the rock leans out on nearly every side, expect steep, powerful moves rather than slab. The landings are described as friendly, and the boulder is only a short stroll from where you park, which makes it an easy first stop before exploring the quieter blocks nearby on this less crowded mountain.

sd_red_light_district.blurb: Red Light District is a limestone sport wall in the Mohican section of Spearfish Canyon, tucked between Purgatory and the Head Shop Wall. It has eleven bolted lines, and the grades lean hard: one easy route, a couple around 5.10 and 5.11, then a cluster of seven in the 5.12 range and a single 5.13. The wall is big, with a large overhang at its base where the stone can be crumbly, so check holds as you go. It suits strong climbers looking for steep, pumpy leads rather than beginners, and it sits near some of the canyon's best-regarded walls.

sd_far_downs.blurb: Far Downs is a small granite formation among the Tolkien-themed spires of Middle Earth, near Sylvan Lake in Custer State Park. It lies just west of Erebor and is easiest to reach by the trail heading downhill from Near Downs. About eleven routes are here, mostly traditional with a pair of bolted lines, running from around 5.7 to 5.11 with the greatest number in the 5.10 range. The north face stays shaded through summer, which is welcome in heat, and the summit views are said to rival the best in the Needles. Middle Earth sees far fewer climbers than the neighboring Outlets, so expect quiet.

sd_blowin_kisses_wall.blurb: Blowin' Kisses Wall is a limestone sport wall in the Danks section of Spearfish Canyon. It is the first wall you meet after turning right at the Hangover Wall, roughly a five-minute walk in. Around eleven bolted routes span the 5.9 to 5.13 range, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 band, so it works for intermediate climbers up through strong ones. The Danks as a whole features long, pumpy lines on very featured stone. A handy man-made belay platform at the wall's most popular route makes it comfortable for the person on the ground.

sd_fishbowl_the.blurb: The Fishbowl is the far-left wall of Blue Sky in Spearfish Canyon, a limestone sport crag with eleven routes between roughly 5.10 and 5.13. Most climbs fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The wall is vertical to slightly overhanging, with small bulges near the top and holds that are mostly pockets and edges. Trees shade it, so it can feel cold on a sunny winter day. A walk of three to five minutes along the main trail from the Blue Sky approach brings you to the base, and the easiest line there makes a popular warm-up before the harder climbs.

sd_light_bulb_buttress.blurb: Light Bulb Buttress is a limestone sport crag in the Sunshine zone of Spearfish Canyon. Eleven bolted routes climb a steep dark face, a dihedral with a pocketed yellow face, and more dark stone on the buttress to the right. The grades run from about 5.8 to 5.12, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and a few 5.11s above it, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on moderate-to-hard pocketed faces. Sunshine is known as a good spot on warm winter days.

sd_calm_area_the.blurb: The Calm Area is a small cluster of granite boulders on the back side of Mount Baldy, in the Needles of Rushmore near Mount Rushmore. Its eleven problems sit on three main blocks and run from solid V4 and V5 up through the V8 to V11 range, so there is little here for beginners. Most lines are well-rated, and a couple of the V4s are the area's most popular. The boulders sit down a gully on the left side from the main Baldy area, and finding the way can take local knowledge. The gully is also home to one of Baldy's hardest problems.

sd_horcrux_wall.blurb: Horcrux Wall is a bouldering wall in the Horsethief Lake area of the Needles of Rushmore, South Dakota, part of the Shrieking Shack Boulders. The formation runs a good length and tops out on large, slabby ledges. Its eleven problems range from easy V1 and V2 lines through V3 and V4 to a handful of hard V6 to V9 problems, so it works for a mixed group. Park at the Big Pine Trailhead across from the campground entrance, then walk a short way along the front of the first formation. The wall sits around the corner from the road, and there is room for more hard lines.
